newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Dec 10.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Works Ltd is expected to post a current profit of more than 500 million yen in the business year to November 1997, up four percent from the same period a year earlier. It is also expected to increase its consolidated net profit by four percent to more than 29 billion yen, helped by strong sales of construction materials spurred by an increase in luxury housing construction.

Survey by the Bond Underwriters Association of Japan shows that bond issuance by Japanese companies in Japanese and overseas markets is expected to total more than 11 trillion yen in calendar 1996, the first time in three years it will exceed 10 trillion yen. Record-low interest rates have inspired companies to refinance old debt, and deregulation of the bond markets has also contributed to increased issuance.

Fujitsu Ltd plans to change terms of contracts with its suppliers, seeking to enhance electronic data interchange (EDI) and to comply with new regulations on intellectual property and product liability (PL). Fujitsu wants suppliers to use the industry standard EDI system.

Mitsubishi Motors Corp and India's leading vehicle maker Hindustan Motors Ltd have given up a plan to commission a local unit of General Motors Corp to manufacture Mitsubishi subcompact passenger cars in India. The two companies had reached an agreement with GM's Indian unit this autumn to manufacture about 10,000 Mitsubishi Lancers a year from the beginning of 1998.
